info.description:
Household task management API.

Conventions callers need:
- Every response is the envelope `{ success, message, data }`.
- `user`, `group` and `task` are addressed by opaque `uid`; every other resource by numeric `id`.
- Timestamps are UTC with no zone suffix — parse as UTC, convert for display.
- Actors are derived from the token; never send a user or member id to identify the caller.
- Errors: 400 validation, 401 unauthenticated, 403 forbidden, 404 not found, 409 duplicate or violated business rule, 429 rate limited (see `Retry-After`).
- Role requirements are stated per operation and are not modelled in this spec.

ChangePasswordRequest.description: Request body for "change password": the current password plus the chosen new password.

ConnectedAccountsResponse.description:
The caller's sign-in methods: whether a password is set and whether a Google account is linked.
 At least one is always true for an active account (otherwise it couldn't sign in).

googleLinked.description: true if a Google account is linked

passwordSet.description: true if the account has a password

DeactivateAccountRequest.description:
Request body for "deactivate account". The password is required for an account that has one
 (re-authentication) and ignored for a Google-only account, which the valid session confirms.

ErrorResponse.description: The standard envelope, as returned for a failed request.

ForgotPasswordRequest.description: Request body for "forgot password": the email to send a reset link to.

GoogleAuthRequest.description: Request body for "Sign in with Google": the Google ID token plus the OIDC nonce secret.

GroupResponse.description:
A group as returned by the API. The invite code is a shareable join secret, so it is exposed
 only through {@link com.tasklean.api.domain.group.dto.GroupResponse#withInviteCode(Group) #withInviteCode(Group)} — for callers allowed to invite.

MyGroupResponse.description:
A group as seen by one of its members, carrying that member's own role so a client can decide
 which admin controls to show. The invite code is present only for a group admin.

NotificationSettingEntry.description:
One entry of a batch update — the same shape the GET returns, so a client can send back the
 list it rendered. Unlike the single-type endpoint, the type travels in the body.

NotificationSettingRequest.description:
Request body for one notification type's channels — a full replace of that entry, so both
 channels are required. The type itself comes from the path, never the body.

NotificationSettingResponse.description: One notification type's delivery channels for the caller.

inApp.description: whether it appears in the in-app notification list

NotificationSettingsBatchRequest.description:
Request body for a batch update: each entry fully replaces that type's channels. Types the
 batch omits are left untouched.

RecoveryCodesResponse.description:
A freshly generated set of recovery codes. Only ever returned once - they are stored hashed, so
 they cannot be shown again.

recoveryCodes.description: the single-use codes, in the order they should be displayed

ResetPasswordRequest.description: Request body for "reset password": the emailed token and the chosen new password.

SetPasswordRequest.description: Request body for "set password" on a Google-only account: the chosen new password.

TwoFactorConfirmRequest.description:
Request body for an operation that weakens or replaces an active second factor (turning it off,
 regenerating recovery codes): both the account password and a current second-factor code, so
 neither a stolen session nor a stolen password is enough on its own. The password is required
 for an account that has one and ignored for a Google-only account.

TwoFactorEnableRequest.description:
Request body for confirming setup: the code currently shown by the authenticator app that was
 just enrolled. No password - the pending secret itself is the proof.

TwoFactorEnableResponse.description:
The result of turning two-factor on: the one-time recovery codes, plus a fresh session for the
 current device because enabling signs every other device out.

recoveryCodes.description: the single-use codes, shown to the user only here

refreshToken.description: the new refresh token for the current device

token.description: the new access token for the current device

TwoFactorSetupRequest.description:
Request body for starting two-factor setup. The password re-authenticates the caller; it is
 required for an account that has one and ignored for a Google-only account, which the valid
 session confirms.

TwoFactorSetupResponse.description:
What the client needs to enroll an authenticator app. The factor is not active yet - it becomes
 active only once a code from it is confirmed.

otpauthUri.description: the otpauth://totp/... URI to render as a QR code

secret.description: the Base32 secret, for manual entry when a QR code can't be scanned

TwoFactorStatusResponse.description: The caller's two-factor state, enough for the settings screen to decide what to show.

confirmedAt.description: when the factor was confirmed; null while it isn't enabled

enabled.description: true if a confirmed second factor is required at sign-in

pendingSetup.description:
true if setup was started but never confirmed, so the client can
                                offer to resume it

recoveryCodesRemaining.description: how many unused recovery codes are left; 0 when not enabled

TwoFactorVerifyRequest.description:
Request body for finishing a sign-in that needs a second factor: the opaque challenge token the
 login response returned, plus a code from the authenticator app or one recovery code.

UserSettingsRequest.description: Request body for replacing the caller's settings — a full PUT, so both fields are required.

locale.description: the UI language (lowercase the name for the BCP-47 tag)
